questions.q: What is the capstone scenario asking you to secure?
options: Every system Northbridge Retail owns
Northbridge Retail's order-service pipeline, end to end
Only the production database
A brand-new service with no existing pipeline
questions.explain: The capstone is deliberately scoped to one service — order-service — and its existing, currently-unsecured pipeline, not the entire organization.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the six required controls for the capstone pipeline?
options: SAST
Dependency scanning
A full SIEM deployment
Least-privilege deploy identity
questions.explain: The six required controls are SAST, dependency scanning, secrets scanning, image scanning, a policy gate, and a least-privilege deploy identity. A full SIEM is explicitly called out as out of scope for this capstone.

questions.q: What does the policy gate control do?
options: It scans source code for syntax errors
It blocks the pipeline from proceeding if any required scan reports a finding above an agreed severity threshold
It automatically patches any vulnerability it finds
It replaces the need for a deploy identity
questions.explain: The policy gate is the single automated checkpoint that enforces the other scan results — it blocks progression when findings exceed the agreed threshold, rather than performing a scan itself.

questions.q: Why does the lesson insist all six controls are required, rather than treating some as optional extras?
options: Because more controls always look better on a resume
Because each control catches a category of problem that none of the others catch, per the cumulative security principle from Lesson 4
Because the course requires exactly six slides per lesson
Because Northbridge Retail's auditors mandate exactly six checks
questions.explain: This directly reuses the Lesson 4 cumulative security idea: a threat model won't catch a leaked dependency, and a dependency scan won't catch a leaked secret. Skipping one leaves a real gap, not a smaller project.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against also adding runtime security or a full disaster-recovery plan to the capstone?
options: Because those topics are not real or valuable
Because they are out of scope for this project, and a finished, focused six-control pipeline is a stronger result than an unfinished, broader one
Because Northbridge Retail does not use runtime security anywhere
Because those topics were never covered anywhere in this course
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly scopes the capstone to keep it finishable, warning that an unfinished fifteen-control pipeline is a weaker portfolio piece than a complete six-control one.
